video.title: Why I Switched to Base44 in 2026 (Full Honest Review)

summary: Mikey No Code explains why he moved from Lovable to the AI app builder Base44 in 2026. He says Lovable was good for prototypes but became costly and fragile once projects needed databases, authentication and backend logic, because small changes caused regressions that burned credits. He demos a tech-summit app (Event Pulse) with a database, bookmarking, authentication, a private portal and a redesign. He says Base44 kept everything working and built it in under 15 minutes. The video is largely a product review and also promotes his own Base44 master class, so the claims are one-sided and promotional.

tactics.name: Test an AI builder incrementally, not with one big prompt
steps: Add a live database feature such as bookmarking
Add authentication and a private portal
Run a full redesign and check mobile
Re-test that data, login and state still work after each step

quote.text: A single generation does not really tell you much about context retention or stability
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Decide whether to switch builders with three questions
steps: Does the product need secure accounts, persistent data and background automation?
Is more time and credit going on repairs than on new features?
Is the goal a live business product rather than full control of the source code?
If all three are yes, switching is justified

tactics.name: Use a free giveaway course as a lead magnet in videos
steps: Put a link to the course in the description
Frame the normally $499 course as free for viewers
Repeat the call to action mid-video and at the end

warnings.warning: Base44 may be a poor fit if you need fully portable source code or two-way Git sync.

quote.text: Some teams want full two-way git synchronization and the freedom to take the code out of the platform
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Don't switch platforms just because they are newer; moving only makes sense if current problems cost more than the move.
Static landing pages and simple prototypes gain little from switching, and specialised stacks may not fit Base44's entity system.

lessons.lesson: Judge AI builders by how well an app survives the 4th to 10th change, not by the first generation.

quote.text: What matters is whether their project still holds together after generation 4, five, or 10
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Regression repairs quietly drain credits; track how much budget goes on fixing versus new features.
Production client apps need integrated database, auth and hosting; each extra service adds failure points and subscriptions.
Separating credits for building from credits for runtime backend activity makes costs easier to predict.
Background agents that run on a schedule turn an app into a business process that keeps working without a user present, which suits automation-first businesses.
Switching tools has a real cost in muscle memory and migration, so set an explicit checklist before switching.
Treat creator tool reviews as marketing when the creator sells courses about the tool.

evidence_quality.rationale: Promotional product review from a creator who sells a Base44 course. The single demo is first-hand but small and unverified, with no business revenue figures, and the transcript has some garbled passages.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sells a Base44 master class (normally $499, given free via the link) and promotes it repeatedly in the video.
